# Brandthread mobile app — full QA audit (report only)

_Audit date: 2026-10-06. Scope: the Expo/React Native app (seller + buyer), its web preview, and the API calls it makes. No app code was changed._

## Summary

**1471 findings** — **P0: 6**, **P1: 168**, **P2: 586**, **P3: 711**.

| Severity | Count | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| P0 | 6 | crash / data loss / broken flow |
| P1 | 168 | broken feature / wrong behavior |
| P2 | 586 | visual / UX |
| P3 | 711 | polish |

Findings by category: visual/UX 838, accessibility 218, web-preview 113, code 97, security/preview 74, app-store 46, layout 28, state 23, api 9, web/a11y 9, copy 5, console 5, performance 2, forms 1, resilience 1, dead control 1, tooling 1.

Findings by evidence source: visual 838, crawl 366, code 209, appstore 46, manual 11, tap 1 (visual = screenshot review, crawl = automated route crawl, tap = tap-every-control crawl, code = source review, appstore = App Store review audit, manual = hand-tested).

## Top 30 — fix these first

1. **Sign-up crashes when the Terms gate appears** (P0, QA-0005) — LegalAcceptanceGate calls a hook after `return null`; React throws the moment an Apple/Google sign-up needs to agree to Terms. Verified in the live Repl file.
2. **In-app calls are fake** (P0, QA-0002, QA-0006) — Buyer and seller DM call buttons use the simulated preview provider unconditionally: it rings and 'connects' to nobody.
3. **Boosts, ads and Featured slots are sold through Stripe on iOS** (P0, QA-0001, QA-0003, QA-0004) — Digital promotions bypass Apple IAP (the IAP flag isn't set in the repo; may exist in the EAS dashboard). Near-certain App Store rejection.
4. **Signed-out preview calls 74 protected API endpoints** (P1, QA-0010, QA-0014, QA-0015, …) — Seller profile, store, products, subscription, moderation, etc. are requested with no session (401). Breaks the house rule and is why many preview screens show 'Couldn't load' / 'Unauthorized'.
5. **Paid AI endpoints slip past the signed-out guard** (P1, QA-0102, QA-0127) — The guest guard's `ai` prefix doesn't match `ai-helpers`; caption generation can fire from the preview (server still requires sign-in).
6. **Package presets API was never mounted** (P1, QA-0156) — `routes/index.ts` imports the router but never `use()`s it, so Shipping's package presets always 404.
7. **Checkout routes show the home feed** (P1, QA-0007, QA-0012) — /buyer-checkout and /thread-checkout open the feed with the gesture tutorial instead of a checkout or empty-cart state.
8. **Delete account shows a raw 'Unauthorized' and a dead Continue** (P1, QA-0069, QA-0070) — Buyer and seller Delete-account screens greet the user with a raw error; review risk for account deletion (5.1.1(v)).
9. **App Review demo accounts can't delete themselves** (P1, QA-0072) — Their seeded paid 'processing' orders block deletion.
10. **Account deletion doesn't cancel the seller subscription** (P1, QA-0073) — No cancellation and no App Store billing warning.
11. **'Manage subscription' opens Stripe's portal on iOS** (P1, QA-0167) — External purchase steering (3.1.3).
12. **Subscription screen says both 'Free' and '$29/mo'** (P1, QA-0166, QA-0093) — Current plan card and plan list contradict; Finance also shows Starter $29/mo for sellers with no subscription.
13. **Seller Orders is empty in demo while Dashboard shows orders to ship** (P1, QA-0119) — Two screens contradict each other in the same demo session.
14. **Fresh accounts show sample data** (P1, QA-0087, QA-0054, QA-0077, QA-0078, QA-0157, QA-0038) — Edit profile, Brand, Discover (Just Dropped / Trending Brands), Shopping preferences and Activity show demo content without &demo=1.
15. **'Block undefined' in conversation Privacy & safety** (P1, QA-0128, QA-0131) — Name missing in the block row and helper copy; nickname screen has the same gap (QA-0117).
16. **Live feed fakes actions** (P1, QA-0111, QA-0108, QA-0109) — Thread Cash send reports success without calling the API; chat and Follow are local only.
17. **Shared live and creator-program links 404** (P1, QA-0110, QA-0147) — Copied /live/<id> and /creator-program/join links have no matching route.
18. **Push/notification consent gaps** (P1, QA-0148, QA-0057) — Seller follower broadcasts skip the promotional opt-in; buyer Notifications settings are a local mock with seller toggles.
19. **AI tools send personal photos to a third party without disclosure** (P1, QA-0043) — No in-app consent for sending user content to the AI provider (5.1.2(i)).
20. **Vacation mode can silently reopen the store** (P1, QA-0173, QA-0172) — A failed load shows 'off', and Save then wipes the away message; there is also an unlabeled white button.
21. **Billing says 'Owner access required' to the store owner** (P1, QA-0048, QA-0049) — Demo and fresh sellers are locked out of Billing.
22. **Store builder renders a broken white block** (P1, QA-0161) — Unstyled wireframe instead of the builder in seller demo.
23. **Publish your store and Share profile are blank** (P1, QA-0136, QA-0149) — No checklist or Publish button; no QR or link.
24. **Domains: subdomain is device-only and self-verified** (P1, QA-0081, QA-0080) — Save writes AsyncStorage only; the demo subdomain section is empty.
25. **Broken param wiring between screens** (P1, QA-0082, QA-0113, QA-0126, QA-0042) — Drop push notifications pass ?id= but the screen reads dropId; Marketing passes campaignId but the screen reads id; Boost ignores targetId; the canvas ignores AI Studio's size and import.
26. **Discounts take free-text dates** (P1, QA-0076) — Invalid input throws, end-before-start is allowed, and expiry falls on the wrong day.
27. **/activity opens 'Not found'** (P1, QA-0118) — Seller route resolves to a missing screen.
28. **Payout schedule shows the next payout in the past** (P1, QA-0122) — 'around Oct 1' on Oct 6 with a Daily schedule.
29. **IP report submit is unreachable** (P1, QA-0140) — The submit button stays behind the tab bar even at the end of the scroll.
30. **Production web bundle is a single 12.8 MB JS file** (P2, QA-0757, QA-0758) — 3.4 MB gzipped, and ~46 MB of demo videos ship in every build (see the performance findings).

## How this audit was done (read this — environment caveats)

- **Target.** The brief asked to audit the live Replit preview. This cloud container's network policy only allows package registries, so `*.replit.dev` and `replit.com` were unreachable. Instead the live Repl's code was reconstructed locally: `origin/dev` + every open PR that the Repl contains (PRs #533–#688; #689–#692 are **not** in the Repl), then every file that conflicted between PRs (117 files) and every Repl-only file (14) was copied verbatim from the Repl through the Replit connector. Nine files over the connector's 100 KB read limit (`lib/api.ts`, `app/_layout.tsx`, `app/onboarding.tsx`, `app/design-canvas.tsx`, `app/order-detail.tsx`, `app/seller-conversation.tsx`, `app/buyer-conversation.tsx`, `app/(tabs)/feed.tsx`, `lib/db/src/schema/index.ts`) were merged locally and hand-repaired; behavior that depends only on those files is the least certain part of this report.
- **Running it.** Expo web dev server (`expo start --web`, `__DEV__` on, like the Replit preview) + the real API server + a local Postgres with all 224 migrations. API calls were proxied same-origin like on Replit. Clerk's script cannot load here (fake key domain) — the preview modes don't need it; anything that only breaks because Clerk is absent was excluded.
- **Coverage.** All 362 routes × 4 modes (seller demo `?bt_preview=seller&demo=1`, seller fresh `?bt_preview=seller`, buyer demo `?bt_preview=buyer&demo=1`, buyer fresh) at 390×844 with a screenshot at the top and after scrolling to the end; the 70 primary screens again at 375×667 and 430×932; every control tapped on 70 primary seller/buyer screens; scripted flows (add product validation, search, add to cart/checkout, keyboard, signed-out entry); network + console captured everywhere; 1,100+ unique screenshots reviewed visually; source review of the whole app; every P0/P1 static claim re-verified against the live Repl source.
- **Static P0/P1s were verified.** 130 static P0/P1 claims were re-read in the live Repl: 126 confirmed, 4 refuted (dropped). Each verified item says so under "Verified".
- **Not bugs here.** Black video tiles (the test browser has no H.264 codec); Expo dev "Uncaught Error: Clerk" overlays; anything in the excluded areas below.
- **Excluded on purpose (other sessions own them):** studio menu polish, camera-first Create, dashboard Add-a-product/setup card/Content Analytics header, back/cancel/X return targets, Analytics + Reports + Best time to post, header subtitle/divider + tab-bar/notch clearance sweep (content actually hidden behind the bar is still reported), seller profile header + profile empty states, seller vs buyer Messages, Products/Orders chips/sort/filter empty states, and the upcoming restyle (font, cards, icons, caps, motion, neon).
- **"web-preview" platform tag.** `Alert.alert` is a no-op in react-native-web, so confirm-dialog flows that work on iOS are dead in the web preview. Those are tagged `web-preview` and capped at P2.
- **Stopped early (time box):** the tap-every-control crawl covered about 55 of 70 primary screens. Its automatic "dead button" results proved unreliable because of tap timing, so only manually re-verified dead controls are reported. 38 second-level detail pages (order/product/conversation/story/seller-profile with real demo IDs) were crawled and screenshotted but not reviewed visually; they appear only through automated checks. No finding was re-checked on the live Replit preview, which this environment cannot reach. Every finding carries a **Verified** line that says how it was checked; static P2/P3 code findings are marked **UNVERIFIED** against the live Repl.
- **Screenshots** are in `docs/audit/screens/` (64-colour PNGs). File names: `<MODE>__<route>[__bottom].png`, MODE = S1 seller demo, S0 seller fresh, B1 buyer demo, B0 buyer fresh, `s` suffix = 375×667, `L` = 430×932, FLOW/MAN = scripted/manual.

**Seller app** — floating tab bar: Dashboard `/` · Products `/products` · Orders `/orders` · Profile `/profile`, plus the centre Studio button `/studio` (radial menu: Create, Live, Design, Store, Marketing, Finance, …). Settings: Profile → gear `/settings` → `/seller-settings`.

**Buyer app** — floating tab bar: Home `/` (Following / Threads feed) · Discover `/discover` · Inbox `/inbox` · Profile `/profile`; Cart `/cart`, Orders `/orders`, Activity `/activity`, Friends `/friends` are pushed from those tabs. Settings: Profile → menu `/buyer-settings-menu`.

**Preview entry** — `?bt_preview=seller` / `?bt_preview=buyer` (dev/preview hosts only, never production), `&demo=1` for the populated dataset; read once on load and mirrored into `localStorage.user_role` / `bt_preview_demo`.

## Findings

Sorted P0 → P3, grouped by screen. Each finding: ID · severity · what's wrong · steps · expected · likely source · screenshot. `findings.json` has the same data, machine-readable.

### P0 — crash / data loss / broken flow (6)

#### Boost post (seller)

- **QA-0001** · P0 · app-store — **On iOS, boosts are paid through Stripe Checkout instead of IAP unless a build flag is set**
  - What: nativePromotionsEnabled() returns true only when EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS==='1'. That variable is not set in eas.json or anywhere else in the repo. In a production iOS build nativeRail is false, so the boost purchase (paid in-app visibility, a digital service used inside the app) opens a Stripe Checkout session in an auth browser. The screen also says 'Secure payment via Stripe. You'll be redirected to complete payment.' This breaks Guideline 3.1.1, and showing an external payment mechanism breaks 3.1.3.
  - Steps: Seller account > Studio/Marketing > Boost a post > pick a post and budget > 'Boost post · $X' > Stripe Checkout opens in a browser sheet.
  - Expected: On iOS/Android, buy boosts only as App Store/Play consumables through RevenueCat. Ship with EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS=1 and the consumables created, or hide paid boosts on native.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/lib/iapPromotions.ts:37-42; artifacts/mobile/app/boost.tsx:458,787,1176-1178`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. nativePromotionsEnabled() requires EXPO_PUBLIC_IAP_PROMOTIONS==='1' and Repl eas.json sets no such env (production profile uses EAS 'environment: production', so it could only come from EAS dashboard env vars, not visible in source); boost falls back to Stripe openAuthSessionAsync and shows the Stripe copy.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Buyer conversation (/buyer-conversation) - voice/video call

- **QA-0002** · P0 · code — **Calls are fully simulated in production: fake ring, fake "connected", nobody is called**
  - What: CallSessionContext hard-wires `const provider = createPreviewCallProvider()` (no network, no media). The header phone/video buttons are shown to every signed-in buyer (gated only on conv && !isAgentConv); an outgoing call "rings" for 2.2s then auto-connects and later shows "{name}'s camera is off", while the other person receives nothing. Call-log bubbles are then written into the thread. Note: a real Agora engine already exists at app/call-screen.tsx (used by manufacturer messages), so DMs are the only path left on the simulator.
  - Steps: Signed-in buyer, open a DM with a seller, tap the phone icon; have the seller watch their device.
  - Expected: Hide call buttons until a real provider (Agora) is wired, or place a real call.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/lib/calls/CallSessionContext.tsx:25; artifacts/mobile/lib/calls/previewCallProvider.ts:1-75; artifacts/mobile/app/buyer-conversation.tsx:722-735,2236 (local)`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. CallSessionContext hard-wires `const provider = createPreviewCallProvider()` (Repl line 25); the preview provider auto-connects after RING_MS=2200 and sets peerCameraOff after 4s with no network or media, and call logs are only local context state; the buyer-conversation gating (conv && !isAgentConv, line 2236) was checked in the local copy since that file is >100KB.
  - Evidence: code review

#### Create ad (seller)

- **QA-0003** · P0 · app-store — **In-feed ad campaigns are paid through Stripe Checkout on iOS (same flag defaults to off)**
  - What: design-campaign.tsx uses the same nativePromotionsEnabled() rail. With the flag unset, 'Launch · $X' opens Stripe Checkout (WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync). The ads are Brandthread in-feed placements shown inside the app, which makes them a digital service. Guidelines 3.1.1 and 3.1.3.
  - Steps: Seller > Marketing > Create ad > fill in creative and budget > Launch > Stripe Checkout opens.
  - Expected: Sell through IAP consumables on native, or don't offer paid ad campaigns on iOS.

#### Featured on Discover (seller)

- **QA-0004** · P0 · app-store — **Paid 'Featured' slots are always sold through Stripe Checkout, with no native IAP path**
  - What: featured-slot.tsx has no IAP rail at all. pay() reserves a slot and opens Stripe Checkout with WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync on every platform. Prices are $29/$59/$99 for in-app promotion on the Discover tab, which is a digital service consumed in the app. Guideline 3.1.1.
  - Steps: Seller > Boost screen > 'Featured' entry (boost.tsx:1069) > choose 3/7/14 days > 'Pay $29' > Stripe Checkout opens.
  - Expected: Use an IAP consumable/non-consumable on iOS and Android, or hide the feature on native.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/featured-slot.tsx:124-142`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. featured-slot.tsx pay() always reserves then opens Stripe Checkout via openAuthSessionAsync with no Platform/IAP branch; demo prices are $29/$59/$99.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Legal agreement gate (post sign-in)

- **QA-0005** · P0 · app-store — **LegalAcceptanceGate calls a hook after an early return; it crashes when the gate needs to show**
  - What: LegalAcceptanceGate returns null when needsAgreement is false, then calls useIsWebShell() (which calls useWindowDimensions) after that return. On first render needsAgreement=false, so the hook is skipped. When check() sets needsAgreement=true, the next render runs one more hook and React throws 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render'. The React Compiler skips components that break the rules of hooks, so it does not fix this. The gate shows for every account without a recorded agreement. That includes anyone who signs up with Apple or Google from the sign-in screen, which never stores pending consent. So the first launch after Sign in with Apple crashes, or lands on the root ErrorBoundary. Guideline 2.1 (crash), and the 1.2 EULA agreement never completes.
  - Steps: Fresh install > Sign in > Continue with Apple using a new Apple ID > the account is created > the gate's check() finds no termsVersion > re-render > crash or error screen.
  - Expected: Call every hook before any conditional return (move useIsWebShell above `if (!isSignedIn || !needsAgreement) return null`). The agreement modal should then render.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/components/legal/LegalAcceptanceGate.tsx:100-107`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Repl has `if (!isSignedIn || !needsAgreement) return null;` at line 100 followed by `const isWebShell = useIsWebShell();` at 107, so hook count changes when needsAgreement flips true.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Seller conversation (/seller-conversation) - voice/video call

- **QA-0006** · P0 · code — **Seller call buttons start a simulated call that auto-"connects" with no one**
  - What: Same preview-only provider: seller voice/video icons (rendered whenever an id exists) start a fake call that auto-connects after RING_MS; the buyer is never rung. Callback from a call-log bubble does the same. Note: a real Agora engine already exists at app/call-screen.tsx (used by manufacturer messages), so DMs are the only path left on the simulator.
  - Steps: Seller opens a buyer DM, taps the video icon; check the buyer's device.
  - Expected: Real call or no call buttons.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/lib/calls/CallSessionContext.tsx:25; artifacts/mobile/app/seller-conversation.tsx:627-640,1232 (local)`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Same preview-only provider; the seller-conversation startCall (line 629) and CallLogBubble onCallBack (line 1232) were checked in the local copy (file >100KB), so seller calls auto-'connect' without ringing anyone.
  - Evidence: code review

#### AI Settings (/ai-settings)

- **QA-0041** · P1 · code — **Most AI settings toggles have no effect (data sources, enable assistant, confirmations, suggestions)**
  - What: Settings are saved only to AsyncStorage and the only field read anywhere is sessionMemoryEnabled (services/aiService.ts). "Enable AI assistant", "Dashboard suggestions", "Brand Memory", all confirm-before-action toggles, and every Data source toggle (Products, Orders, Customers, ...) are never consulted, so turning off e.g. Customers does not stop the assistant from using customer data. Also device-local only, so they don't follow the seller to another device.
  - Steps: AI Settings -> turn off "Customers" data source and "Enable AI assistant"; open AI Brain and ask about customers.
  - Expected: Toggles enforced (ideally server-side) and synced to the account.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/ai-settings.tsx:203-210; artifacts/mobile/services/aiService.ts:65-77,129-130,169-170`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. ai-settings only writes to AsyncStorage (saveAISettings); in aiService the only setting consulted is sessionMemoryEnabled (loadSession/_persistSession), buildChatRequest always sends getEnabledMemorySummary() regardless of brandMemoryEnabled, and nothing reads enabled/suggestionsEnabled/confirm*/dataSources (local repo grep shows no other readers).
  - Evidence: code review

#### AI Studio (/ai-studio) -> Design canvas

- **QA-0042** · P1 · code — **New canvas size and imported artwork are ignored by the canvas**
  - What: openCanvas and importFromLibrary push /design-canvas with params { label, dims, ratio, imageUri }, but design-canvas reads only { id, addAssetId }. Picked canvas size is lost and the imported image never appears.
  - Steps: AI Studio -> New canvas -> choose a size; or Import from library and pick an image.
  - Expected: Canvas opens at that size with the imported image as a layer.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/ai-studio.tsx:68,80; artifacts/mobile/app/design-canvas.tsx:289 (local copy)`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Repl ai-studio openCanvas/importFromLibrary (and openFromCamera) push /design-canvas with { label, dims, ratio, imageUri }; design-canvas is >100KB so it was checked in the local copy, where it reads only { id, addAssetId } (line 289) and never references imageUri/dims/ratio.
  - Evidence: code review

#### AI tools (seller): AI Studio, Photoshoot, Background removal, Text-to-design, Assistant

- **QA-0043** · P1 · app-store — **Personal data is sent to a third-party AI provider without any in-app disclosure or consent**
  - What: The privacy policy says prompts and selected content (including users' photos) are sent to 'our AI providers'. The server calls OpenAI (bg-removal, photography, mockup and other routes). No screen in the app asks for consent or explains this before the first upload: there is no AI consent string or flag anywhere in app/, components/ or lib/. Guideline 5.1.2(i) requires clear disclosure, and explicit permission, before personal data goes to a third-party AI.
  - Steps: Seller > Studio > AI Studio / AI photoshoot > upload a photo of a person > generate. There is no consent sheet.
  - Expected: Show a one-time consent sheet naming the AI provider and the data sent, record the acceptance, and allow opting out.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/content/legal/privacy.md:41,56; artifacts/mobile/app/design-bg-removal.tsx:11,263-268`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. privacy.md lines 41/56 disclose AI providers only in the policy; design-bg-removal.tsx posts the photo to /api/bg-removal/remove with no consent prompt, and no AI-consent flag was found (app-wide absence checked against local copy).
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Delete account (reviewer demo accounts)

- **QA-0072** · P1 · app-store — **The seeded App Review accounts cannot delete themselves because their seeded orders block it**
  - What: The review seed creates order 1004 as paid and 'processing', plus order 1003 as shipped 4 days ago. getDeletionBlockers() blocks a buyer with paid orders in pending/processing ('buyer_orders_awaiting_shipment'). It blocks a seller with paid orders not yet delivered that shipped less than 30 days ago. Both demo accounts therefore see 'Settle these first' with Continue disabled. REVIEW_NOTES.md tells reviewers deletion works from Settings > Delete account. Guideline 5.1.1(v).
  - Steps: Sign in as the demo buyer (or seller) > Settings > Delete account > the blocker card appears and Continue stays disabled.
  - Expected: Seed the review accounts with no open obligations (e.g. only delivered or cancelled orders), or let deletion proceed and auto-cancel/refund instead of blocking.
  - Source: `artifacts/api-server/src/scripts/reviewDemo/plan.ts:183-184; artifacts/api-server/src/lib/accountDeletion.ts:56-104`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. Seed plan has RVW-1004 'processing' (paid) and RVW-1003 'shipped' 4 days ago; getDeletionBlockers blocks buyer on paid pending/processing orders and seller on paid undelivered orders (shipped <30d), so both demo accounts get blockers (1004 blocks both even once 1003 ages out).
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Delete account (seller with subscription)

- **QA-0073** · P1 · app-store — **Deleting an account does not cancel the seller subscription or warn about App Store billing**
  - What: purgeAccount() deletes seller_subscription_entitlements rows but never cancels the Stripe subscription. Nothing in accountDeletion.ts or accountPurge.ts calls subscriptions.cancel. The deletion screen's 'What we delete / keep' lists and blockers never mention an active App Store or Play subscription, which keeps renewing after the account is gone. Apple expects apps to tell users how to cancel subscriptions billed through Apple (5.1.1(v), 3.1.2).
  - Steps: Seller on a paid plan > Settings > Delete account or store. There is no warning about the subscription. After 30 days the account is purged and Stripe or Apple keep charging.
  - Expected: Cancel Stripe subscriptions when deletion is scheduled. For App Store/Play subscriptions, show a notice with a link to manage or cancel in the store.
  - Source: `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/accountDeletion.ts:221-260; artifacts/api-server/src/jobs/accountPurge.ts; artifacts/api-server/src/routes/auth.ts:299-308`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. purgeAccount only deletes seller_subscription_entitlements and nulls subscriptionId; neither it nor jobs/accountPurge.ts (path is src/jobs/, not lib/) cancels Stripe/store subscriptions, and the server-provided willDelete/willRetain lists (routes/auth.ts:299-308) never mention subscriptions.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Delete account (Sign in with Apple / Google users)

- **QA-0074** · P1 · app-store — **Passwordless accounts can only delete with an emailed code, which may fail to arrive**
  - What: getReauthMethod() returns 'email_code' for every account without a password (all Apple and Google sign-ups). issueDeletionCode() fails with MAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED when Resend is not set, and with MAIL_SEND_FAILED on a send error. For 'Hide My Email' Apple users the code goes to a privaterelay.appleid.com address and is dropped unless the sending domain is registered with Apple's Private Email Relay. Any of these leaves the user stuck at 'Enter the 6-digit code'. There is no fallback such as a fresh Apple re-auth. Guideline 5.1.1(v).
  - Steps: Sign in with Apple using Hide My Email > Settings > Delete account > Continue > 'Email me a code' > no email arrives, so deletion cannot be finished.
  - Expected: Use a native re-auth for SSO accounts (re-run Sign in with Apple/Google, or check Clerk's recent session), and register the mail domain with Apple's Private Relay.
  - Source: `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/accountDeletion.ts:321-323,376-403; artifacts/mobile/app/delete-account.tsx:88-104`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. getReauthMethod returns 'email_code' whenever passwordEnabled is false; issueDeletionCode fails with MAIL_NOT_CONFIGURED/MAIL_SEND_FAILED and the delete screen offers no alternative re-auth (Private Relay delivery is an external-config risk, not verifiable in code).
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Domains (/store-domain) - Brandthread subdomain

- **QA-0081** · P1 · code — **Subdomain "Save" only writes AsyncStorage and self-marks it verified**
  - What: handleSaveSubdomain calls storeService.updateDomain, which edits the local storefront and calls saveStorefront; that function persists to AsyncStorage and fire-and-forgets api.store.save with a payload that has no domains/subdomain field. The new subdomain never reaches the server, is marked verificationStatus 'verified' locally, and "Saved / Subdomain updated." is shown anyway.
  - Steps: Domains -> change subdomain to "newname" -> Save; open https://newname.brandthread.app or sign in on another device.
  - Expected: Subdomain claimed via the API (with availability check) or the field is read-only.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/store-domain.tsx:83-95; artifacts/mobile/services/storeService.ts:429-463,835-841`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. handleSaveSubdomain calls updateDomain(btDomain.id, { subdomain, verificationStatus: 'verified' }), which only edits the local storefront and calls saveStorefront (AsyncStorage plus a fire-and-forget api.store.save payload with no domains/subdomain field), then shows 'Saved / Subdomain updated.'
  - Evidence: code review

#### Guest API guard (lib/guestApiPolicy.ts) - affects signed-out preview

- **QA-0102** · P1 · code — **Paid AI helper endpoints slip past the signed-out guard ("ai" prefix doesn't match "ai-helpers")**
  - What: SIGNED_IN_ONLY_PREFIXES contains 'ai' and matching is `p === prefix || p.startsWith(prefix + '/')`, so '/api/ai-helpers/caption', '/product-description' and '/size-chart' (postExpensive AI calls) are not blocked. Also not listed: 'posts/<id>/captions/generate' (AI captions), 'products/images' upload, 'seller/profile/*/upload', 'communities/upload-photo', 'seller/subscription/checkout' (Stripe). The house rule says signed-out preview must never hit paid/protected APIs.
  - Steps: In signed-out web preview, trigger any of those calls (e.g. Generate captions on /post-captions-edit) with devtools Network open.
  - Expected: All paid/AI/upload/Stripe paths are short-circuited client-side when there is no token.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/lib/guestApiPolicy.ts:10-29; artifacts/mobile/lib/api.ts:1180-1185,1203,2576 (local copy)`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. SIGNED_IN_ONLY_PREFIXES has 'ai' and matching is p===prefix || p.startsWith(prefix+'/'), so 'ai-helpers/*', 'posts/<id>/captions/generate', 'products/images', 'seller/profile/*/upload', 'communities/upload-photo' and 'seller/subscription/checkout' are not short-circuited (api.ts checked in the local copy since it is >100KB); the server still 401s them (e.g. ai-helpers router.use(requireAuth)), so this is a client-guard gap, not an actual paid call.
  - Evidence: code review

  - What: The server builds programLink as `${webOrigin}/creator-program/join?brand=<username>` (api-server routes/seller-affiliate.ts:57) and the seller copies it here, but the app route is /creator-program-join (app/creator-program-join.tsx reads ?brand). No /creator-program/join route or rewrite exists, so creators opening the link hit Not Found.
  - Steps: Seller -> Creator program -> Copy program link -> open in a browser.

  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. The Repl server builds programLink as `${getWebOrigin()}/creator-program/join?brand=...` (seller-affiliate.ts:57), and the Repl's app/ has only creator-program-join.tsx with no creator-program/ directory (serve.js has no rewrite in the local copy), so the copied link hits Not Found; the copy call at seller-creator-program.tsx:126 was checked in the local copy.
  - Evidence: code review

#### Seller follower push broadcast

- **QA-0148** · P1 · app-store — **Seller marketing broadcasts skip the promotional-push opt-in**
  - What: deliverBroadcast() publishes each broadcast with type 'seller_broadcast' and category 'announcements', and sets no pushKind. PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES does not include 'seller_broadcast' or 'announcement', so isPromotionalPush() returns false. promoConsentAllows() then lets the push through to every follower even when promo_push_opt_in=false. A seller-to-follower blast is marketing. Guideline 4.5.4 requires explicit opt-in.
  - Steps: Seller > Marketing > Push broadcast > send. A follower who never enabled promotional notifications still gets the push.
  - Expected: Pass pushKind:'promotional' in deliverBroadcast, or add 'seller_broadcast' to PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES.
  - Source: `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/sellerPushBroadcast.ts:244-257; artifacts/api-server/src/lib/pushPolicy.ts:15-25`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. deliverBroadcast publishes type 'seller_broadcast'/category 'announcements' with no pushKind, and PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES lacks 'seller_broadcast', so promoConsentAllows returns true regardless of promo_push_opt_in (audience filter only checks push_enabled and seller_announcements pref).
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Subscription management (seller)

- **QA-0167** · P1 · app-store — **'Manage subscription' opens the Stripe billing portal in a browser on iOS**
  - What: handleOpenPortal() has no platform check. When the subscription's effectiveProvider is 'stripe' (a seller who subscribed on the web), getBillingRecoveryTarget returns 'stripe' and the app opens api.seller.subscription.portal() with Linking.openURL on iOS. In the Stripe customer portal the user can change plans, upgrade and update cards. That is an external purchase mechanism reached from the app (Guidelines 3.1.1 and 3.1.3). billing.tsx already blocks this on native, so the two screens disagree.
  - Steps: Sign in on iOS as a seller who subscribed on web > Settings > Subscription > 'Manage subscription' or 'Manage billing' > Safari opens the Stripe portal.
  - Expected: On native, never open the Stripe portal. Show 'Manage your plan at brandthread.app' as plain text (no link), or use the App Store management URL only for RevenueCat subscriptions.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/subscription.tsx:208-223`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. handleOpenPortal() has no Platform check; when getBillingRecoveryTarget returns 'stripe' it opens api.seller.subscription.portal() via Linking.openURL on native too.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

- **QA-0224** · P2 · app-store — **Platform-wide announcement pushes skip the promotional opt-in**
  - What: deliverAnnouncement() calls sendPushToUser for every user in the audience with data.type 'announcement' and no kind. That type is not in PROMOTIONAL_PUSH_TYPES, so announcements are always treated as transactional. Any marketing announcement would break Guideline 4.5.4.
  - Steps: Admin sends an announcement with sendPush=true. Users who opted out of promotional notifications still receive it.

#### Blocked accounts (/buyer-blocked)

- **QA-0249** · P2 · web-preview · `web-preview` — **Unblock account never completes on web**
  - What: Uses lib/safety.ts confirmBlock/confirmUnblock or lib/actionSheet.ts confirmDestructiveActionSheet, which on non-iOS fall back to Alert.alert with button callbacks (lib/safety.ts:143,172; lib/actionSheet.ts:36). On react-native-web Alert.alert is a no-op, so the returned Promise never resolves (onDismiss never fires either): no dialog, no block/unblock, and the awaiting handler hangs.
  - Steps: In the web build open /buyer-blocked and tap Unblock account.
  - Expected: A confirmation appears on web and the block/unblock/delete is performed (or cancelled) and the promise resolves.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/buyer-blocked.tsx:72`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. unblock() sets pendingId then awaits confirmUnblock (Alert.alert-only in lib/safety.ts:172); on web the promise never resolves, so the button spins forever and all other Unblock buttons stay disabled; works on iOS.
  - Evidence: code review

  - Expected: A confirmation appears on web and the block/unblock/delete is performed (or cancelled) and the promise resolves.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/conversation-details.tsx:251-252`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. openOptions uses web-safe showActionSheet, but its Block/Unblock item then awaits confirmBlock/confirmUnblock (Alert.alert-only in lib/safety.ts), which never resolves on web; works on iOS.
  - Evidence: code review

#### Conversation privacy & safety (/conversation-privacy-safety)

  - What: Uses lib/safety.ts confirmBlock/confirmUnblock or lib/actionSheet.ts confirmDestructiveActionSheet, which on non-iOS fall back to Alert.alert with button callbacks (lib/safety.ts:143,172; lib/actionSheet.ts:36). On react-native-web Alert.alert is a no-op, so the returned Promise never resolves (onDismiss never fires either): no dialog, no block/unblock, and the awaiting handler hangs.
  - Steps: In the web build open /conversation-privacy-safety and tap Block / Unblock.
  - Expected: A confirmation appears on web and the block/unblock/delete is performed (or cancelled) and the promise resolves.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/conversation-privacy-safety.tsx:46-47`
  - Verified: Verified against the live Repl source: confirmed. toggleBlock awaits confirmBlock/confirmUnblock, which in lib/safety.ts:143/172 call Alert.alert unconditionally with button/onDismiss callbacks, so on web the promise never settles and nothing happens; works on iOS.
  - Evidence: code review

- **QA-0353** · P2 · app-store — **Apple tokens are never revoked when an account is deleted**
  - What: The deletion handler and the purge job delete the Clerk user, but nothing calls Apple's /auth/revoke endpoint for Sign in with Apple users (no revoke code in api-server). Apple expects apps that offer Sign in with Apple to revoke tokens on account deletion (5.1.1(v), Sign in with Apple account-deletion requirements).

- **QA-0370** · P2 · web-preview · `web-preview` — **Block / Unblock from DM safety banner never completes on web**
  - What: Uses lib/safety.ts confirmBlock/confirmUnblock or lib/actionSheet.ts confirmDestructiveActionSheet, which on non-iOS fall back to Alert.alert with button callbacks (lib/safety.ts:143,172; lib/actionSheet.ts:36). On react-native-web Alert.alert is a no-op, so the returned Promise never resolves (onDismiss never fires either): no dialog, no block/unblock, and the awaiting handler hangs.

#### Publish store (/store-publish)

- **QA-0576** · P2 · code — **Publish/unpublish errors unhandled; URL falls back to fake "yourstore.brandthread.app"**
  - What: publishStore() exceptions are not caught (only finally), so a network failure produces an unhandled rejection and no message; unpublishStore() has no try at all and flips the UI to unpublished before knowing it succeeded. When settings.storeUrl is empty the screen and the confirmation promise the store will be live at "https://yourstore.brandthread.app". The URL is also taken from settings.storeUrl while the Domains screen edits domains[].subdomain, so the two screens can show different store addresses.
  - Steps: Publish while offline; or publish a store with no storeUrl; or change the subdomain on Domains and compare with Publish.
  - Expected: Error feedback; real URL from one source of truth; no placeholder hostname.
  - Source: `app/store-publish.tsx:117-160 ; app/store-domain.tsx:55,87`
  - Verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.

#### Sign in screen

- **QA-0680** · P2 · app-store — **The sign-in screen creates accounts through Apple/Google with no Terms or Privacy link and no consent stored**
  - What: sign-in.tsx offers 'Continue with Apple' and 'Continue with Google'. With Clerk SSO these create brand-new accounts. The screen has no LegalContinueNotice, no Terms/Privacy link and never calls rememberPendingConsent(). New users from this path get no agreement until the LegalAcceptanceGate, which currently crashes (see the P0 finding). Guidelines 1.2 (EULA before UGC) and 5.1.1(i) (privacy policy reachable at sign-up).
  - Steps: Fresh install > Sign in > look for Terms/Privacy links next to the Apple/Google buttons.
  - Expected: Show the same 'By continuing you agree to…' notice with tappable Terms, Privacy and Guidelines links on the sign-in screen.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/sign-in.tsx:687-725`
  - Verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Sign up (onboarding)

- **QA-0681** · P2 · app-store — **Agreement to the EULA and community rules is browsewrap, with no affirmative action**
  - What: Account creation records consent implicitly: rememberPendingConsent() runs on 'Continue' and the screen shows a LegalContinueNotice line. LegalAcceptanceGate then sends that stored pending consent to the server automatically, so the user never actively agrees to the zero-tolerance terms. Reviewers often ask for an explicit agreement to the terms or EULA in UGC apps (Guideline 1.2).
  - Steps: Fresh install > Create account > email/password > Continue. There is no checkbox or 'I agree' step.
  - Expected: Add an explicit checkbox or 'I agree' tap before account creation for UGC users.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app/onboarding.tsx:668-673,973,1049,1475; artifacts/mobile/components/legal/LegalAcceptanceGate.tsx:48-55`
  - Verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit

#### Whole app (web build / app size)

- **QA-0757** · P2 · performance — **Production web bundle is one 12.8 MB JS chunk (3.4 MB gzipped)**
  - What: `expo export --platform web` of the current code produces a single 12.8 MB `index-*.js` (3.41 MB gzipped) that every visitor downloads before first paint; the remaining 4 chunks are <50 KB, so route-level code splitting is effectively not happening. On a mid-range phone over 4G this is several seconds of download + parse before the first screen.
  - Steps: `pnpm --filter @workspace/mobile exec expo export --platform web` and inspect `dist/_expo/static/js/web`.
  - Expected: Lazy route bundles (Expo Router async routes) so the first screen ships < 1 MB gzipped; heavy screens (Design Studio, AI, Live, Manufacturer) load on demand.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app.json (web.output / asyncRoutes), artifacts/mobile/metro.config.js`
  - Evidence: build measurement
- **QA-0758** · P2 · performance — **~46 MB of demo-feed videos ship inside the app bundle**
  - What: Ten `assets/videos/fashion_runway_*.mp4` files (4.4–5.0 MB each) are `require()`d statically by the preview/demo feed data, so they are bundled into every build (web export assets total 103 MB; they would also inflate the iOS binary/OTA update) even though they are only shown in demo/preview mode.
  - Steps: Build the web export or an iOS archive and list bundled assets.
  - Expected: Demo media served from a CDN (or excluded from production builds); production bundle contains no demo-only media.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/lib/previewFeed.ts and other preview*.ts files that require ../../assets/videos/*.mp4`
  - Evidence: build measurement

#### Contacts permission prompt

- **QA-0972** · P3 · app-store — **The contacts purpose string says contacts are 'never uploaded', but hashed contacts are uploaded**
  - What: NSContactsUsageDescription says 'your contact list is never uploaded or stored'. The app hashes every email and phone and POSTs up to 6,000 SHA-256 hashes to /api/social/contacts/match. Unsalted hashes of phone numbers can be reversed, and the privacy manifest declares Contacts as collected. The privacy policy never mentions contacts. Guideline 5.1.1 (accurate purpose strings and policy).
  - Steps: Read the iOS permission prompt and compare it with the network traffic from Find friends.
  - Expected: Reword to 'only scrambled codes (hashes) are sent to check matches and aren't stored', and add contact matching to privacy.md.
  - Source: `artifacts/mobile/app.json:383-387; artifacts/mobile/lib/contactHashing.ts:1-14; artifacts/mobile/content/legal/privacy.md`
  - Verified: UNVERIFIED against the live Repl (only P0/P1 static claims were re-checked); found in the reconstructed source.
  - Evidence: App Store review audit
